title: Aether Vanguard: fixing the first turn in an AI-assisted browser card game
author: Fluffy-Play1251
selftext:
I'm building Aether Vanguard, a free browser card game, with AI-assisted code and narrative text and AI-generated visual assets. A recent playtester said the opening story and instructions took too long before they could do anything.



The AI-assisted change was deliberately small: send new guests straight to the existing guided match, shorten its first instruction, and keep the story accessible from How to Play. The regression test performs a real first-card drag, then checks that optional story access still works without resetting progress. Desktop and phone checks passed before deployment.



In a local clean-browser test, following the automatic opening went from 31.84 seconds to the first usable card to 2.47 seconds. The old opening already had a Skip button, so that comparison is about the default path, not every player's experience. One feedback report and a faster test do not establish a retention improvement.



Playable build: [https://theredwizard.net/aethervanguard/](https://theredwizard.net/aethervanguard/)



If you try one match, where did you first hesitate, and what did you think should happen next? I'm also interested in how other developers validate AI-assisted onboarding changes beyond an automated happy path. Guest play needs no account or download, and real-money purchases are unavailable.

comments.author: KazThe10th
comments.body:
https://preview.redd.it/vt4tcfyariqh1.jpeg?width=1320&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=2223e8d16e15d4dfbcab293347b84d93444a3308

  
1. This is confusing. Text says Gilded Hall but the lane says Muster Yard. 

2. On the next move you mention Lumen Knight but the card in the pic still says Aether Sentinel. It also says Quiet Meadow but the middle lane is titled Shield Walk. It’s only after that is dismissed that you see Lumen Knight is a card in hand that is to be played next. 

3. Next turn still has a picture of Aether Sentinel. Confusing since you’re talking about a different card. And the terms you use there “far spire” when the lane is titled East Stair is confusing. 

4. The constant pulsing/warping of the opponent’s cards makes them hard to read. 

5. Theres no way to see your cards without pulling up each one individually. So everything the text is talking about requires more calories to figure out. 

I like games like this so I can see where you’re going. The issue is a tutorial and the foundational game should be frictionless.

comments.author: SupMekBots
comments.body:
I’m building an AI-assisted mecha card game, and I took a similar approach to the first match. After a short story introduction, players are guided through a few core mechanics before getting full control. I also use an in-world virtual assistant to explain things instead of relying on popups.

I’m also curious about the business side... since it runs in the browser, how are you planning to monetize it?
